run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only failing user path in hotel-reservation is the recommendation path: the frontend's HTTP GET /recommendations returns 500 because its gRPC client call /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations fails immediately (18-81 us), and no recommendation server span exists. GET /hotels and all of its downstream dependencies (search, geo, rate, profile, reservation) still return 200 with normal sub-millisecond/ few-millisecond spans. The fault object is the NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation in namespace hotel-reservation: its podSelector matches io.kompose.service=recommendation, its policyTypes are Ingress and Egress with no rules at all (deny all traffic to and from those pods), and it was created at 2026-11-23T22:05:32Z - 3 seconds after the recommendation container had registered srv-recommendation (10.244.7.204:8085) in Consul and 1 second before the current frontend pod started; every sampled GetRecommendations call after that (20 of 20, 22:05:40-22:05:43) failed. The recommendation pod itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, but the deployment defines no probes, so Ready does not reflect reachability, and the deny-all policy also blocks its egress to mongodb-recommendation and to the tracing collector, which is consistent with the complete absence of recommendation spans in Jaeger. Checked and healthy: search, geo, rate, profile, reservation, user and the frontend /hotels path. Rejected candidates: a rate-service QPS/queue fault (rate RPCs succeed, RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=500, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256) and the geo/rate MongoDB admin-privilege fault scripts (no auth errors; geo and rate completed DB init and wrote test data at startup). The rate:9091 scrape failure at 22:05:44 was a startup artifact (target health up, lastError empty at 22:06:59). Because the environment was created only at 22:05:18-22:05:33 there is no pre-incident baseline for this instance.

claims.text: Impact: the frontend operation HTTP GET /recommendations returns HTTP 500. In a sample of 20 traces (22:05:40-22:05:43) all 20 HTTP GET /recommendations spans of service frontend carry error=true and http.status_code=500, and all 20 matching client spans /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations carry error=true (otel.status_code=ERROR).

The failing client span fails fast: /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations durations are 18-81 us and its parent HTTP GET /recommendations span completes in 38-123 us, i.e. the failure happens without waiting on the remote service; the span carries no error_detail text.

A full trace lookup of a failing request (trace_id 514fb69a1224da49) contains exactly two spans, both in service frontend: the HTTP GET /recommendations 500 server span and its child client span /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations in error; no span from the recommendation service appears.

Jaeger's service list for this target is exactly frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search, user - the recommendation service has never recorded a span, which is consistent with its egress to the tracing collector being blocked.

The NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation exists in namespace hotel-reservation with podSelector matchLabels io.kompose.service=recommendation and policyTypes [Ingress, Egress]; both spec.ingress and spec.egress are absent/null, i.e. all ingress and all egress traffic for the recommendation pods is denied and nothing is allowed.

The deny policy's creationTimestamp is 2026-11-23T22:05:32Z and its only managedFields entry is manager OpenAPI-Generator, Update, at 2026-11-23T22:05:32Z (no later write recorded), so the policy was created inside the incident window and no subsequent modification is recorded.

The recommendation container had already registered itself in Consul before the deny policy existed: pod recommendation-86cf75495d-97lbr (IP 10.244.7.204) logged 'Trying to register service [ name: srv-recommendation, id: fbbebd91-..., address: 10.244.7.204:8085 ]' and 'Successfully registered in consul' at 22:05:29Z, and the Consul pod logged the corresponding PUT /v1/agent/service/register from 10.244.7.204 at 22:05:29.099Z.

The recommendation pod is not visibly crashed or misconfigured: recommendation-86cf75495d-97lbr is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination state, its pod IP 10.244.7.204 matches the address registered in Consul, and the recommendation Service endpoints contain 10.244.7.204:8085.

The recommendation Deployment container hotel-reserv-recommendation defines no livenessProbe or readinessProbe (its container spec carries only name, command [recommendation], args -jaegeraddr otel-collector.observe.svc.cluster.local:6831, env JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1, port 8085 and the image), so the pod's Ready condition does not test that the gRPC port is reachable.

Other user paths are healthy, so the fault is not frontend-wide: in a sample of 10 traces each, HTTP GET /hotels returned http.status_code=200 (3.0-5.6 ms) and its children /search.Search/Nearby, /geo.Geo/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles and /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability were served by those services with 0 error rows.

Rate-service QPS/queue saturation was considered and rejected: the rate deployment runs with RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=500 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256, the rate pod started cleanly and registered as srv-rate (10.244.7.203:8084) with no restarts, and traces show /rate.Rate/GetRates client and server spans succeeding in 12-1180 us with 0 error rows.

The MongoDB admin-privilege fault shipped in ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo (revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh / remove-admin-mongo.sh on geo-db) and failure-admin-rate (revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh on rate-db) was considered and rejected as a cause here: geo logged 'New session successfull...' and 'Generating test data...' and rate logged the same plus 'New session successfull...' after connecting to mongodb-*:27017, and mongodb-rate logs contain no authorization or authentication error lines in the window.

The rate:9091 metrics scrape failure seen at 22:05:44 is not evidence of a rate fault: up{instance=rate.hotel-reservation:9091,job=hotel-reservation-application} was 0 at 22:05:44, but the same scrape target is health=up with lastError empty and lastScrape 22:06:59, so it was a startup artifact of a pod started at 22:05:20.

The blackbox probe signals cannot be used to size the impact: probe_success was 0 at 22:05:44 for all nine hotel-reservation probe instances, including frontend:5000, geo:8083, rate:8084, profile:8081, reservation:8087, search:8082 and user:8086, while traces show those same services serving requests successfully.

The whole namespace is younger than the incident window: every one of the 19 hotel-reservation pods has creationTimestamp between 22:05:18Z and 22:05:32Z, and events show all deployments scaled up from 0 at that time, so no behaviour of this app instance exists before 22:05:18 in the collected data.

A second change occurred in the same window: the frontend Deployment (generation 2) was updated by manager kubectl-rollout at 2026-11-23T22:05:32Z, its ReplicaSet frontend-68745cb99c was deleted and frontend-6bdb659d9b created at 22:05:32-22:05:33Z with the same image digest sha256:1c685e1c..., i.e. a restart without an image change.

Mechanism: the deny-all-recommendation NetworkPolicy (created 22:05:32Z) blackholes the frontend's gRPC traffic to recommendation-86cf75495d-97lbr 10.244.7.204:8085, so the frontend's long-lived gRPC channel is in a failed state and each GetRecommendations RPC aborts in tens of microseconds, producing HTTP 500 on /recommendations; the same policy's egress denial also prevents the recommendation container from reaching mongodb-recommendation:27017 and otel-collector.observe:6831, which is consistent with recommendation never appearing in Jaeger.

Inspect and, if unintended, remove or correct NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation in namespace hotel-reservation so the recommendation pods regain ingress on 8085 and egress to mongodb-recommendation:27017 and the tracing collector, then re-test GET /recommendations.
Add a gRPC/TCP readiness probe on port 8085 for the recommendation Deployment, because the pod currently reports Ready with no probe while the service was unreachable.

gaps: No CNI/kube-proxy evidence or client error text was available (the failing client span carries no error_detail fields), so whether the deny policy results in silent drop or connection refused on the frontend-to-recommendation path is unverified.

The recommendation process's own health beyond container Running/Ready cannot be observed: its logs stop at 22:05:29Z (registration) and no recommendation spans exist, so whether it was listening on 8085 at 22:05:40Z is unknown.
Who or what created the NetworkPolicy is recorded only as managedFields manager 'OpenAPI-Generator'; the change_history integration is not available, so the actor and intent are unknown.
The frontend Deployment rollout by kubectl-rollout at 22:05:32Z with an unchanged image digest is unexplained; no evidence ties it to the /recommendations failures, and its trigger is unknown.
There is no pre-22:05:18 data for this app instance, so no latency or error baseline exists for comparison and recurrence cannot be assessed.

Probe configuration content is not observable; all nine blackbox-hotel-reservation/blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probes return probe_success=0 including endpoints proven working by traces, and the ingress probe returns probe_http_status_code 0 while no Ingress object exists in the namespace, so probe results were not used as impact evidence.

The rate service application metrics (rate_requests_received_total, rate_requests_completed_total, rate_requests_rejected_total, rate_requests_expired_total, rate_queue_depth, rate_in_flight, rate_backend_qps_limit, rate_queue_capacity) had no samples inside the queried window, so rate's internal queue/QPS behaviour is unknown rather than zero.

search_rate_attempts_total=52, search_rate_successes_total=51, search_rate_failures_total=1, search_rate_timeouts_total=0 is a single-window reading with no baseline, so whether that one failure is background or meaningful is unknown.
Only 20 recommendation-call traces were sampled; the failure rate across all requests is not established, only that every sampled call in 22:05:40-22:05:43 failed.
next_steps: Review the deny-all-recommendation NetworkPolicy with the team that owns fault injection, confirm whether it is still intended, and remove it if not.

Verify from a pod in the namespace (for example a temporary netcat/grpcurl check from an allowed pod) that recommendation:8085 is reachable after the policy change and that recommendation can reach mongodb-recommendation:27017.
Compare this deployment with the reference hotel-reservation manifests to confirm the deny-all policy is not part of the intended baseline.

Fix the blackbox probe targets for the hotel-reservation services (all currently report probe_success=0 for endpoints that serve traffic) and add a gRPC-aware readiness probe to the recommendation Deployment.
Ask why the frontend Deployment was rollout-restarted at 22:05:32Z and whether that restart was part of the same injection procedure.

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
